newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria cuts imports forecast, sees trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: Algeria cuts imports forecast, sees trade surplus.

text.p: Algeria on Wednesday forecast a current account surplus of $300 million by the end of 1966, reversing a forecast of a $2 billion deficit, an official statement said.
The statement, carried by the official news agency APS after a cabinet meeting, said total imports in the first half of the year fell by 15 percent, giving a surplus trade balance of $1.3 billion.
No figures were given for total exports for the period from the North African country which earns 94 percent of foreign income from oil and gas sales abroad.
In June this year, official figures showed total exports, mainly of oil and gas, reached $10.240 billion for the whole of 1995 compared with $8.501 billion for all of 1994.
Imports in 1995, according to the earlier figures, were put at $10.761 billion, against $9.365 billion in 1994.
Wednesday's statement said non-energy exports rose by 53.4 percent to $366 million in the first six months of 1996.
It said imports fell because of a good harvest, recession and stagnation in the industrial sector, and a drop in the purchasing power of Algeria's 29 million people.
"The drop of costly food imports alone attained 29 percent compared with the previous year," the statement said.
Non-energy industrial production fell by 7.4 percent in the first six months of 1996, compared with the whole of the previous year for which no figure was given.

"The hydrocarbon sector in the first half of 1996 saw a growth rate of eight percent compared with the first half of the previous year, notably because of an increase of gas production -- up 8.1 percent -- growth of condensate production up 6.6 percent, growth of refined products up 3.7 percent, and the reinforcement of gas liquefaction, up 15.1 percent.
